name: Jadeheart Sanctuary
reason: The source faction 'Jade Pure Holy Land' (also rendered 'Jade Pure Sacred Ground') was renamed 'Jadeheart Sanctuary' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A Tier-Ten Holy Land in the upper world that Zane encounters after ascending (Eps 1252-1320). It is a dominant power whose ranked Palace Masters command wide recognition; its Ninth Palace Master is a woman of the Divine Transformation realm. Those who ascend without connections in the Jadeheart Sanctuary are at a disadvantage, and falling into its hands is feared.

name: Lava Giant
reason: The source creature term 'Lava Giant' was carried over unchanged, as it already suits the Western fantasy register.
description: Colossal magma creatures encountered in Eps 1291-1295, with fists the size of small buildings and crushing charging speed. They prey on the flame kittens living around a lava lake; Zane's group (Janet, Coleman, Hailey and Jeffrey) battles them, including a clash between two Lava Giants fighting over a flame kitten.

name: Timothy
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Tianhu' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Timothy' for the Western setting of the adaptation.
description: A clan fighter of the Tower of Sin arc, ranked twenty-second among his clan's seat controllers and serving under the group's leader (Eps 631-1062). He handles field duties such as producing the golden Scorchplate scale the Flaming Place provided (source: Tianhu's Flaming Balance) and fights alongside Shane in the Twilight Group; his crew is outmatched by Esther and the top War Lords from Demon Night.

name: Septuplets
reason: The source group 'Void Spirit Seven' / 'Seven Masters of the Void Spirit Sect' was renamed the 'Septuplets' of the Ethereal Spirit Sect, replacing the literal numbering with a Western term for a seven-member unit.
description: The seven elite masters of the Ethereal Spirit Sect (source: Void Spirit Sect), who fight as a unit arrayed in the pattern of the Big Dipper (Eps 454-728). Their combined strength is said to rival Cloud Hall, they shone at the Martial Arts Conference decades ago, and they later cooperate with Zane in a trap against Maddox (source: Cui Xie).

name: Stoney
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhao Heiyan' was fully localized; 'Stoney' was chosen as a blunt, menacing nickname-style name fitting this pale, sadistic minor antagonist.
description: A pale-faced, sickly-looking warrior recently broken into the Core-Forged Realm, notorious for holding grudges and for slaughtering an entire Second-Grade sect (Eps 462-470). He wields the Discipline of Vile Malice and its Skull Ghost Hand (source: Zhao Heiyan's 'Great Hatred Demon Attack' and Heavenly Spirit Ghost Claw), a soul-crushing ghostly-hand attack. When he strikes at a seemingly defenseless Zane in the illusion-array trials, the attack backfires and Zane dispatches him with complete indifference.

name: Nexus Point
reason: The source's traditional Chinese medicine term 'acupoint' (e.g. the Baihui acupoint tempered with the power of thunder and fire) was renamed 'Nexus Point' to avoid culture-specific anatomy terms in the Western adaptation.
description: Body Refining term: the 108 energy points of the human body that a cultivator refines using Law Power (flame plus lightning), 20 of which sit in the Crown Conduit (Eps 478-487). Channeling the merged energy directly into the Nexus Points is life-threatening for ordinary warriors, yet Zane refines his first in moments - a milestone that should have taken years - and goes on to refine all 108.

name: Brody
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Bu Qiu' was fully localized to a US-origin name; the surname 'Booth' preserves the sound of the original surname 'Bu'.
description: A disciple of Bloodwood Cliff (source: Blood Wood Cliff) and minor antagonist who faces Zane at the Martial Arts Conference (Eps 489-491). He has mastered a third of the Fire Law and fights with the Soul-Killing Poisoned Blood talisman his sect master Lady Darkmere (source: Madam Poison Blood) presses into his chest, but is defeated by Zane.

name: Nameless Saber
reason: The source weapon 'Nameless Buddhist Commandment Blade' was shortened to 'Nameless Saber', dropping the Buddhist reference to fit the adaptation's Western fantasy register.
description: Maddox's (source: Cui Xie's) Relic-Class saber, counted alongside the Ethereal Spirit Sect's Soul Flag and the World Merchants' Guild's Time Copper Coin among the most valuable treasures known in the Heartlands (Eps 492-924). Wreathed in dark tendrils and ancient runes, it summons a Netherworld Fiend when fed blood and can call up the Life and Death Wind from the River of the Netherworld.

name: Craig
reason: The character's name 'Tutulu' (also romanized 'Tuturu') was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Craig' for the Western setting.
description: A young human from the herdsmen storyline whom Zane rescues from captivity (Eps 558-682). Earnest and persistent, he once panicked and shook a little girl for answers until others snapped him out of it, and he repeatedly begs Zane to take him on as a student, undeterred by refusal, drawing chuckles from powerful warriors like Dorian and Amber.

name: Violet Core Physique
reason: The source constitution 'Extreme Purple Yin Body' (also rendered 'Extreme Violet Yin Body') was renamed 'Violet Core Physique', keeping the violet color cue while dropping the yin/yang terminology.
description: A rare female constitution central to the Maddox arc (Eps 681-754): Maddox (source: Cui Xie) needs three women with the Violet Core Physique to complete his Soul Harvesting Ritual (source: activating their Primordial Yin with the Great Demonic Acacia Formation). The physique holds a deep reserve of concentrated energy and is described as the ideal body for dual cultivation; its best-known bearer is the young miss of the Xi Clan (source: Xi Youqin).

name: Kade
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhao Li' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Kade' for the Western setting.
description: A prodigy of the Violet Heart Sanctuary (source: the Human Clan's Purple Heart Holy Land) whose test on the Talent Tablet (source: Talent Tombstone) lights up and outstrips all seven of his seniors (Eps 951-969). His results draw Delroy's visiting faction (source: the Demi-Immortal Clan), which tries to claim him, but the sanctuary makes clear he will not be taken.

name: Master Weaponsmith
reason: The source profession 'Weapon Refiner' was localized as 'Master Weaponsmith', replacing the cultivation-flavored 'refiner' with the Western craft title, in line with the show's 'Cultivator (not refiner)' policy.
description: The prestigious weapon-forging profession of the early arcs (Eps 19-142): in Castermere County a Master Weaponsmith commands fame and fortune unmatched by other professions, and every Legacy House harbors the usually unfulfilled dream of claiming one for its lineage. Zane pursues Weapon Forging partly in the hope that such status would let him see, and save, his sister Elara.

name: Soul
reason: Generic fragment: standalone 'Soul' is a stray token folded from larger terms (Soul Realm masters/warriors, Soul attacks, Soul Flag, Soul Duel, Forging Soul Blades) that are covered by their own entries; it is not a standalone entity.

name: Celestial Library
reason: The source location 'Heavenly Book Pavilion' was renamed 'Celestial Library', a natural Western equivalent for the sect's archive of techniques.
description: The Skyreach Sect's (source: Blue Cloud Sect's) enormous archive of cultivation methods, where deeper access costs contribution points and yields higher-level techniques (Eps 50-288). Zane entered for a trivial hundred points, took the sealed forbidden scroll Titan Strike and somehow mastered it, to the sect's later alarm; he also met the old man known as 'Uncle Kent' there.

name: Ben
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Wang Xufeng' was fully localized to the short US-origin name 'Ben', befitting a minor sect rival.
description: An inner disciple of the Skyreach Sect defending his place in the sect competition (Eps 228-230). His personal best of eighteen thousand points sat comfortably above the eighth-place score of fifteen thousand, so he thought himself safe - until Zane's results threatened to boot him from his spot, leaving him wearing a forced smile.

name: Blood-Corroding Sword
reason: The source weapon 'Corrosive Blood Sword' (Hua Tianming's blade) was lightly reworded as 'Blood-Corroding Sword' for smoother English.
description: Finn Donovan's (source: Hua Tianming's) sword, which replaced his earlier Cyan Blade (Eps 293-382). A unique heirloom whose bloodstains are supposedly thousands of years old and seem to come alive on the blade; Finn pairs it with precise Sword Steps and once condensed an arena-flooding surge of Primal Vitality entirely into it.

name: Celestial Blade
reason: Finn's signature sword art, the source's 'Heavenly Sword' (also rendered 'Sky Sword'), was localized as 'Celestial Blade'.
description: The sword art comprehended by Finn Donovan (source: Hua Tianming), first revealed against Alistair and honed over the years (Eps 295-753). Though Finn is only an Inner-Core Realm warrior, the Celestial Blade's power is said to be on par with a Transcendent Divine Might and strong enough to kill a Spirit-Tribulation Realm master.

name: Adamant Soul
reason: Patrick's Buddhist-flavored source technique, Pei Tianyao's 'Invincible Vajra Body', was renamed the 'Form of the Adamant Soul', removing the vajra reference for the Western register.
description: A golden-light defensive transformation used by Patrick (source: Pei Tianyao) of the Monastic Path (Eps 312-1100). The Form of the Adamant Soul makes the user's body nearly indestructible, but its power flows entirely from the golden light it projects - a dependency opponents can exploit.

name: House Kendrick
reason: The source clan 'Xue Family' was localized as 'House Kendrick', following the show's 'Legacy House' naming convention.
description: A Legacy House whose young master schemed at the Dragon Soar Arena to beat Zane to the ascension portal, backed by three Inner-Core Realm cultivators of the house (Eps 432-451; source: the Xue Family's Young Lord and its Core Formation guards at the Rising Dragon Platform). After the affair, both the young master and the leader of House Kendrick were hauled into Oracle City for questioning.

name: Lady Darkmere
reason: The source title-name 'Madam Poison Blood' was replaced with the invented aristocratic name 'Lady Darkmere', preserving her sinister, venomous persona without the literal 'poison blood' label.
description: Sect Master of Bloodwood Cliff (source: Blood Wood Cliff), a fourth-grade sect, and a Spirit-Tribulation Realm antagonist (Eps 432-542). A glamour specialist whose seductive technique ensnares opponents' will, she schemes around the Dragon Soar Arena, watches Zane's trials with malicious glee alongside Raven, and arms her disciple Brody Booth with a Soul-Killing Poisoned Blood talisman for his match against Zane.

name: Violetwood Sanctuary
reason: The source faction 'Purple Bamboo Holy Land' (also 'Purple Bamboo Sacred Land') was renamed 'Violetwood Sanctuary', keeping the purple-plant imagery in a Western register.
description: A holy-land faction of the Dark World (source: Sifting Yin World), headed by its Sacred Master / Saint Lord (Eps 1126-1166). It stations ranking warriors such as Nyla in Auspice City, collects the Stones from the pavilion's yearly trade with other races, and raised and protected the woman Zane is startled to find within it.

name: Red Dragon
reason: The source's 'red dragon', one of the nine dragons above Qinglong's scales, was carried over literally as 'Red Dragon'.
description: A sentient dragon in Zane's mind and the Cobalt Dragon's seventh brother, awakened as Zane's cultivation deepens (Eps 572-1129). Wry and talkative, he banters with and advises Zane through breakthroughs - though like the Cobalt Dragon he goes quiet during a breakthrough push - once spent five years drawing upon a star in the Great Void, and explains that whoever controls the Ancestral Dragon can command the entire dragon race.

name: Magnus
reason: The source epithet-name 'Celestial Venerable Still Water' was replaced with the strong Western name 'Magnus', fitting his standing as a Supreme Lord.
description: A Supreme Lord (source: Celestial Venerable / Empyrean Still Water), one of the universe's reclusive supreme powers (Eps 1017-1189). He farms tokens from his captive stash of Echo Beasts, rare divine creatures capable of producing them (source: Howling Sky Tapirs producing Roaring Tokens), yet keeps only a little over a hundred on hand. He later becomes one of the five Supreme Lords - alongside Addison of the Ogres and Gunter of the Demon Night - caught in a trap that demands they fight until only one remains, where the sight of a single tempered grain of sand fills him with fear.

name: Frosty Cage
reason: The source item 'Frost Cage' was lightly reworded as 'Frosty Cage' for the adaptation.
description: An expandable ice containment device wielded by Janet (Eps 1289-1294). She springs it open to capture the exhausted flame kitten being hunted by the Lava Giants, then keeps the caged kitten protected as the group fights and flees.

name: Netherworld
reason: The source's Chinese underworld imagery - the 'Yellow Spring' and the Yellow Spring River that leads to hell - was localized as the 'Netherworld' and the 'River of the Netherworld'.
description: The realm of the dead in the show's cosmology, familiar from Heartlands stories about fiends and ghosts (Eps 498-934). Its River of the Netherworld drags sinful souls down into its depths, breeds the Netherworld Fiends, and is the only place where the Life and Death Wind blows - the wind Maddox once summoned through his Nameless Saber.

name: Netherworld Fiend
reason: The source's 'Yellow Spring ghost' summoned by the blade was localized as 'Netherworld Fiend', matching the show's 'Netherworld' naming.
description: A ghostly monster with horns and a saber-sharp tail, born from the abyss of Hell, that finds souls adrift in the River of the Netherworld (Eps 497-499). It is summoned with the wielder's blood through the Nameless Saber and set loose on Zane during the arena match.

name: Runic Tower
reason: The source institution 'Runic Tower' (also rendered 'Rune Tower') was carried over essentially unchanged.
description: The foremost authority on runes in the entire Heartlands (source: Central Domain), to which runemasters flocked as runes evolved under the World Merchants' Guild's rise (Eps 502-748). Its ranked experts display their names in runes on their doors - hanging one upside down is the ultimate public humiliation - and in wartime it dispatches hundreds of runes daily to weave glowing defensive nets across Oracle City.

name: Shaw
issues: Surname collision: this standalone 'Shaw' (Elder Shaw, leader of the Sea Wyrm Sect, Eps 687-773) is a different character from Liam Shaw and Yolande Shaw (Eps 58-145). Do not merge the three under one entity.
reason: The source surname 'Xiao' (Sect Master Xiao of the Fish Dragon Sect) was anglicized to the near-homophone 'Shaw'; the episodes style him 'Elder Shaw'.
description: Leader of the Sea Wyrm Sect (source: Sect Master Xiao of the Fish Dragon Sect), an affable and politically careful sect head (Eps 687-773). He welcomes Zane back after the celestial-tomb rumors of his death and briefs him on the rise of Maddox's Corrupted Divine Kingdom; later, when overwhelming visitors descend on his sect, his fury melts instantly into his most polished smile as he hands over whatever is asked.

name: Wavecrest City
reason: The source location 'River Wave City' was renamed 'Wavecrest City', a more natural English place name that keeps the water imagery.
description: A natural-fortress city to the southeast and one of the Corrupted Divine Kingdom's most critical outposts, garrisoned by its strongest fighters and rumored to host Darius, the kingdom's military advisor (Eps 740-760). Beneath it, tens of thousands of uniformed cultivators pool their Vitality - crushing low-grade Aether Crystals - to fuel a celestial prison controlled by six masters to trap Tia, prompting Zane to fly straight for the city.
